acceptance: Unit tests for decide_required: revert: whose diff deletes a fragment passes; revert: of shipped code with no fragment change is refused under rule (1); `Revert "` follows the owner's choice; feat/fix/perf and ! titles unchanged.
make pr-open accepts a correctly formed revert: PR end to end in tests/unit/scripts/test_pr_landing.py, and the CI changelog check gives the same decision.
description:
scripts/changelog_fragments.py exempts GitHub-style `Revert "..."` titles but not the conventional-commit `revert:` type, which is in neither EXEMPT_TYPES nor REQUIRED_TYPES; when a changed path ships in the package it falls through to "unrecognised title type 'revert'" and requires a fragment, and both make pr-open and the CI changelog check (ci.yml, run from a trusted base copy) refuse. Because --added-files-from counts only added files, deleting the reverted change's fragment never satisfies the check. While landing #4200 (revert of #4196), pr-open refused the `revert:` title; the PR landed as `Revert "..."`. Conversely, `Revert "` skips the fragment even when it reverts a change that already shipped. scripts/trunk_revert.py generates `Revert "` titles.

Decision gate (owner), one rule for both forms: (1) if the diff deletes a changelog.d fragment, the reverted change was unreleased, so no fragment is needed and the deletion satisfies the check; otherwise the reverted change shipped and needs a fragment. Under (1) the owner also decides whether `Revert "` stays blanket-exempt. Or (2) always exempt `revert:` as `Revert "` is today.

Guardrails: keep breaking-title (!) handling; no change to required types feat, fix and perf; pr-open and CI must give the same decision.
